Demi-Trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Les Demi-Trolls, appelés Pertorog au singulier et Pirtereg au pluriel, sont issus du croisement de lignées olog-hai et variags. Plus petits et plus rapides que les Trolls Noirs, ils présentent une silhouette vaguement humaine et une intelligence théoriquement comparable à celle des Hommes.

Ils sont conçus comme gardes d’élite, exécuteurs, champions et chefs de guerre au service d’une puissance de l’Ombre. Leur apparition est surtout associée aux dernières phases du Troisième Âge.

Une création au service de l’Ombre

Ils ne semblent pas avoir émergé spontanément comme peuple autonome. Leur existence résulte d’une sélection ou d’un programme de reproduction imposé par Sauron, des sorciers, des prêtres noirs ou des seigneurs variags. Cette origine explique leur homogénéité physique, l’absence de véritable société indépendante et leur équipement militaire fourni par leurs maîtres.

Différence avec les Olog-hai

Les Olog-hai sont plus grands, lourds et conçus pour briser les lignes. Les Demi-Trolls sont plus rapides, plus agiles, plus humains dans leurs proportions et mieux adaptés au commandement, à la garde ou aux missions spécialisées.

Apparence

Les hommes mesurent en moyenne environ 2,16 m et les femmes près de 2,08 m. Ils possèdent épaules très larges, torse massif, bras puissants, longues jambes, mains énormes et ossature dense.

Leur peau est d’un noir profond et naturellement protectrice. Leurs yeux brillent d’un rouge intense, leur langue est longue et pointue, leur front bas, leur nez large et leur mâchoire très développée.

Longévité et endurance

Ils vivent généralement entre 300 et 500 ans, bien que leur existence soit souvent écourtée par la guerre et les purges. Leur endurance est moyenne relativement à leur masse, mais reste impressionnante selon les standards humains : armure complète, lourdes charges, longues batailles et défense prolongée.

Résistance aux blessures

Leur masse, leur ossature épaisse, leur peau et leur musculature réduisent la gravité des blessures. Ils sont extrêmement difficiles à abattre physiquement, sans bénéficier pour autant d’une résistance exceptionnelle aux enchantements, malédictions, poisons puissants ou contrôles mentaux.

Vision et lumière

Ils voient remarquablement bien dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée dans les ténèbres absolues. Ils préfèrent éviter les lieux vivement éclairés, mais ne craignent pas automatiquement le Soleil et ne se transforment pas en pierre. Une vulnérabilité solaire plus forte peut être prise comme défaut individuel.

Intelligence et éducation

Les sources les décrivent à la fois comme intelligents et comme lents ou stupides. Cette contradiction peut être résolue en distinguant potentiel cognitif et éducation : ils peuvent apprendre tactique, langues et commandement, mais sont élevés exclusivement pour servir et découragés d’agir par eux-mêmes.

Agilité

Ils sont relativement rapides malgré leur taille. Leur corps est mieux proportionné que celui des Olog-hai et adapté à la course, l’escalade, l’équitation, la filature, la dissimulation et l’embuscade.

Une Race sans société propre

Ils ne disposent pas de royaume, de langue ancestrale, de religion autonome ou de familles reconnues. Leur existence est organisée par la forteresse, l’armée et le commandant qui les emploient. Ils peuvent néanmoins développer camaraderie d’unité, rivalités entre compagnies, rites militaires et fidélité personnelle à un chef.

Absence de mariage

Ils ne connaissent pas de mariage traditionnel et ne se reproduisent que lorsqu’une puissance extérieure organise cette reproduction. Les jeunes sont probablement élevés collectivement et séparés selon leurs aptitudes et leur fonction future.

Rapport aux autres Trolls

Ils évitent généralement les Trolls sauvages et entretiennent des rivalités avec les Olog-hai. Ils peuvent les considérer comme des brutes lentes, tandis que les Olog-hai méprisent leur sang humain et leur taille réduite.

Gardes du corps, Exécuteurs et chefs

Leur corps et leur formation les destinent à protéger un maître, bloquer un passage, poursuivre un assassin, écraser une révolte ou terroriser une population. Les plus expérimentés peuvent commander compagnies orcs, mercenaires variags, garnisons et troupes de siège.

Tempérament

Ils sont brutaux, peu curieux, lourdement conditionnés, économes de leurs efforts hors du combat et cruels envers ceux qu’ils dominent. Ils valorisent force, rang, victoire, équipement, approbation du maître et peur inspirée.

Possibilité d’émancipation

Un personnage joueur suppose une rupture exceptionnelle : défaite militaire, destruction de la forteresse, mort du commandant, trahison, abandon ou naissance progressive d’une volonté propre. Cette émancipation ne le transforme pas automatiquement en allié des Peuples Libres.

Religion et langues

Ils ne possèdent aucune religion autonome mais sont instruits dans les rites de l’Ombre et peuvent servir Sauron, un Nazgûl ou un sorcier. Ils parlent le Parler Noir et le westron, puis peuvent apprendre varadja, haradaïque et orquien.

Relations

Ils haïssent particulièrement les Nains, capables de résister à leur charge et de percer leur peau. Les Variags représentent leur héritage humain sans les reconnaître comme parents. Les Orcs les craignent comme officiers et bourreaux. Les Hommes les voient presque toujours comme des monstres ou des armes vivantes.

Vêtements et armures

Ils portent tunique, ceinture, protège-poignets, bottes et cape noirs. Toutes les armures leur sont accessibles, notamment les harnois de métal noir forgés sur mesure. Leur peau naturelle renforce encore cette protection.

Armes et manière de combattre

Ils peuvent manier haches, épées, arcs composites, arbalètes, fléaux, hallebardes, javelots, masses, marteaux, fouets et armes à deux mains, souvent dans des versions surdimensionnées.

Ils combattent comme soldats lourds mais plus mobiles que les Olog-hai : briseurs de ligne, gardes de porte, champions, commandants, protecteurs d’officiers et troupes de contre-attaque.

Équitation et artisanat

Ils peuvent utiliser de puissants chevaux, chameaux du Khand ou montures monstrueuses capables de supporter leur poids. Ils apprennent travail du métal, cuir, empennage, entretien des armes et réparation des armures.

Compétences et talents

Leur formation couvre manœuvres en armure, armes, escalade, équitation, pistage, embuscade, filature, dissimulation, observation, développement corporel, lutte, sprint, commandement, interrogatoire et tactique. Leurs aptitudes mystiques sont limitées et principalement défensives.

Profession

Ils ne produisent normalement que des Combattants. Les spécialisations les plus naturelles correspondent aux rôles de Mercenaire, Éclaireur lourd ou Soldat. Cette restriction doit être conservée sauf décision explicite du MJ.

Une Race sans société propre

Les Demi-Trolls ne disposent pas de royaume, de langue ancestrale autonome, de religion propre ou de traditions familiales indépendantes. Leur existence est organisée par la forteresse qui les abrite, l’armée qui les emploie et l’officier qui les commande. Ils peuvent néanmoins développer des comportements communs au sein d’une garnison : rivalités entre compagnies, respect des vétérans, partage du butin, marques d’unité, rites militaires et fidélité personnelle à un chef.

Absence de mariage

Ils ne connaissent pas de mariage traditionnel et ne se reproduisent que lorsqu’une puissance extérieure organise ou impose cette reproduction. Ils n’ont donc normalement ni familles reconnues, ni héritages familiaux, ni foyers permanents. Les enfants sont probablement élevés collectivement puis séparés selon leur taille, leurs aptitudes et leur fonction future. Cette absence de structure familiale ne signifie pas qu’ils soient incapables d’attachement.

Gardes, Exécuteurs et chefs de guerre

Le rôle de garde du corps est particulièrement adapté à leur nature : encaisser une attaque destinée à leur maître, bloquer un passage, porter une armure très lourde, intimider les visiteurs et combattre plusieurs adversaires. Les Exécuteurs sont entraînés à traquer une cible, éliminer un champion, écraser une révolte ou terroriser une population. Les plus expérimentés peuvent diriger compagnies orcs, mercenaires variags, garnisons, troupes de siège ou unités de Trolls.

Possibilité d’émancipation

Un personnage joueur implique nécessairement qu’un individu puisse au moins partiellement s’affranchir de sa fonction. Une défaite militaire, la destruction de sa forteresse, la mort de son commandant, une trahison ou l’abandon peuvent ouvrir une rupture. Cette émancipation ne le transforme pas automatiquement en allié des Peuples Libres : il peut rester cruel, ambitieux et profondément marqué par son éducation. Son évolution peut consister à découvrir la liberté de choisir, une loyauté non imposée, un but personnel et une identité distincte de celle de ses créateurs.

Équipement spécialisé

Les objets spéciaux sont généralement fournis sur ordre du commandant : arme enchantée, armure noire sur mesure, bouclier renforcé, talisman de protection, monture monstrueuse ou équipement contre la lumière. Cette dépendance à une organisation puissante constitue une limite importante : après la chute de son maître, un Demi-Troll peut conserver un équipement exceptionnel sans disposer des moyens de le réparer ou le remplacer.

Place dans la création de personnage

La Race Demi-Trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg devient disponible à partir du Troisième Âge tardif et peut subsister au Quatrième Âge. Elle doit rester Restreinte en raison de sa puissance, de sa taille, de son association à l’Ombre et de l’absence de société propre.

Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Half-trolls, called Pertorog in the singular and Pirtereg in the plural, are descended from the crossing of Olog-hai and Variag bloodlines. Smaller and faster than Black Trolls, they have a vaguely human silhouette and an intelligence theoretically comparable to that of Men.

They are designed as elite guards, executioners, champions and war leaders in the service of a power of the Shadow. Their appearance is chiefly associated with the final phases of the Third Age.

A creation in the service of the Shadow

They do not seem to have arisen spontaneously as an independent people. Their existence is the result of selection or a breeding programme imposed by Sauron, sorcerers, black priests or Variag lords. This origin explains their physical uniformity, the absence of a truly independent society and the military equipment supplied by their masters.

Difference from the Olog-hai

Olog-hai are larger, heavier and designed to smash battle lines. Half-trolls are faster, more agile, more human in their proportions and better suited to command, guard duty or specialised missions.

Appearance

Men average about 2.16 m in height and women about 2.08 m. They possess extremely broad shoulders, massive torsos, powerful arms, long legs, enormous hands and dense bones.

Their skin is deep black and naturally protective. Their eyes glow an intense red, their tongue is long and pointed, their brow low, their nose broad and their jaw heavily developed.

Longevity and endurance

They generally live between 300 and 500 years, although war and purges often cut their lives short. Their endurance is average relative to their mass but remains impressive by human standards: full armour, heavy loads, long battles and prolonged defence.

Resistance to injury

Their mass, thick bones, skin and musculature reduce the severity of wounds. They are extremely difficult to bring down physically, without possessing exceptional resistance to enchantments, curses, powerful poisons or mental control.

Vision and light

They see remarkably well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. They prefer to avoid brightly lit places but do not automatically fear the Sun and do not turn to stone. A stronger vulnerability to sunlight may be taken as an individual Flaw.

Intelligence and education

The sources describe them both as intelligent and as slow or stupid. This contradiction can be resolved by distinguishing cognitive potential from education: they can learn tactics, languages and command, but they are raised exclusively to serve and discouraged from acting on their own initiative.

Agility

They are relatively fast despite their size. Their bodies are better proportioned than those of Olog-hai and adapted to running, climbing, riding, shadowing, concealment and ambush.

A Race without a society of its own

They possess no kingdom, ancestral language, independent religion or recognised families. Their existence is organised by the fortress, army and commander that employ them. They can nevertheless develop unit camaraderie, rivalries between companies, military rites and personal loyalty to a leader.

Absence of marriage

They know no traditional marriage and reproduce only when an outside power organises that reproduction. The young are probably raised collectively and separated according to their aptitudes and future roles.

Relations with other Trolls

They generally avoid wild Trolls and maintain rivalries with Olog-hai. They may regard them as slow brutes, while Olog-hai despise their human blood and smaller size.

Bodyguards, Executioners and leaders

Their bodies and training suit them to protecting a master, blocking a passage, pursuing an assassin, crushing a revolt or terrorising a population. The most experienced can command Orc companies, Variag mercenaries, garrisons and siege troops.

Temperament

They are brutal, incurious, heavily conditioned, sparing of effort outside combat and cruel toward those they dominate. They value strength, rank, victory, equipment, their master's approval and the fear they inspire.

Possibility of emancipation

A player character requires an exceptional break: military defeat, destruction of the fortress, death of the commander, betrayal, abandonment or the gradual birth of an independent will. Such emancipation does not automatically turn the character into an ally of the Free Peoples.

Religion and languages

They possess no independent religion but are instructed in the rites of the Shadow and may serve Sauron, a Nazgûl or a sorcerer. They speak the Black Speech and Westron, and may later learn Varadja, Haradaic and Orcish.

Relations

They particularly hate Dwarves, who can withstand their charge and pierce their skin. The Variags represent their human heritage without recognising them as kin. Orcs fear them as officers and executioners. Men almost always see them as monsters or living weapons.

Clothing and armour

They wear black tunics, belts, bracers, boots and cloaks. All types of armour are available to them, especially custom-forged harnesses of black metal. Their natural skin further reinforces this protection.

Weapons and fighting style

They can wield axes, swords, composite bows, crossbows, flails, halberds, javelins, maces, hammers, whips and two-handed weapons, often in oversized versions.

They fight as heavy soldiers but are more mobile than Olog-hai: line-breakers, gate guards, champions, commanders, protectors of officers and counter-attack troops.

Riding and craftsmanship

They may use powerful horses, camels of Khand or monstrous mounts able to bear their weight. They learn metalwork, leatherwork, fletching, weapon maintenance and armour repair.

Skills and Talents

Their training covers manoeuvring in armour, weapons, climbing, riding, tracking, ambush, shadowing, concealment, observation, Body Development, wrestling, sprinting, leadership, interrogation and tactics. Their mystical abilities are limited and mainly defensive.

Profession

They normally produce only Fighters. The most natural specialisations correspond to the roles of Mercenary, Heavy Scout or Soldier. This restriction should be preserved unless the GM explicitly decides otherwise.

A Race without a society of its own

Half-trolls possess no kingdom, independent ancestral language, religion of their own or autonomous family traditions. Their existence is organised by the fortress that houses them, the army that employs them and the officer who commands them. They can nevertheless develop shared behaviour within a garrison: rivalries between companies, respect for veterans, division of loot, unit markings, military rites and personal loyalty to a leader.

Absence of marriage

They know no traditional marriage and reproduce only when an outside power organises or imposes that reproduction. They therefore normally have no recognised families, family inheritance or permanent households. Children are probably raised collectively and then separated according to size, aptitude and future function. This absence of family structure does not mean that they are incapable of attachment.

Guards, Executioners and war leaders

The role of bodyguard is particularly suited to their nature: taking a blow meant for their master, blocking a passage, wearing extremely heavy armour, intimidating visitors and fighting several opponents. Executioners are trained to track a target, eliminate a champion, crush a revolt or terrorise a population. The most experienced can lead Orc companies, Variag mercenaries, garrisons, siege troops or units of Trolls.

Possibility of emancipation

A player character necessarily implies that an individual can at least partly break free from an imposed function. Military defeat, the destruction of a fortress, the death of a commander, betrayal or abandonment can create such a rupture. Les Demi-Trolls, appelés Pertorog au singulier et Pirtereg au pluriel, sont issus du croisement de lignées olog-hai et variags. Plus petits et plus rapides que les Trolls Noirs, ils présentent une silhouette vaguement humaine et une intelligence théoriquement comparable à celle des Hommes.

Ils sont conçus comme gardes d’élite, exécuteurs, champions et chefs de guerre au service d’une puissance de l’Ombre. Leur apparition est surtout associée aux dernières phases du Troisième Âge.

Une création au service de l’Ombre

Ils ne semblent pas avoir émergé spontanément comme peuple autonome. Leur existence résulte d’une sélection ou d’un programme de reproduction imposé par Sauron, des sorciers, des prêtres noirs ou des seigneurs variags. Cette origine explique leur homogénéité physique, l’absence de véritable société indépendante et leur équipement militaire fourni par leurs maîtres.

Différence avec les Olog-hai

Les Olog-hai sont plus grands, lourds et conçus pour briser les lignes. Les Demi-Trolls sont plus rapides, plus agiles, plus humains dans leurs proportions et mieux adaptés au commandement, à la garde ou aux missions spécialisées.

Apparence

Les hommes mesurent en moyenne environ 2,16 m et les femmes près de 2,08 m. Ils possèdent épaules très larges, torse massif, bras puissants, longues jambes, mains énormes et ossature dense.

Leur peau est d’un noir profond et naturellement protectrice. Leurs yeux brillent d’un rouge intense, leur langue est longue et pointue, leur front bas, leur nez large et leur mâchoire très développée.

Longévité et endurance

Ils vivent généralement entre 300 et 500 ans, bien que leur existence soit souvent écourtée par la guerre et les purges. Leur endurance est moyenne relativement à leur masse, mais reste impressionnante selon les standards humains : armure complète, lourdes charges, longues batailles et défense prolongée.

Résistance aux blessures

Leur masse, leur ossature épaisse, leur peau et leur musculature réduisent la gravité des blessures. Ils sont extrêmement difficiles à abattre physiquement, sans bénéficier pour autant d’une résistance exceptionnelle aux enchantements, malédictions, poisons puissants ou contrôles mentaux.

Vision et lumière

Ils voient remarquablement bien dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée dans les ténèbres absolues. Ils préfèrent éviter les lieux vivement éclairés, mais ne craignent pas automatiquement le Soleil et ne se transforment pas en pierre. Une vulnérabilité solaire plus forte peut être prise comme défaut individuel.

Intelligence et éducation

Les sources les décrivent à la fois comme intelligents et comme lents ou stupides. Cette contradiction peut être résolue en distinguant potentiel cognitif et éducation : ils peuvent apprendre tactique, langues et commandement, mais sont élevés exclusivement pour servir et découragés d’agir par eux-mêmes.

Agilité

Ils sont relativement rapides malgré leur taille. Leur corps est mieux proportionné que celui des Olog-hai et adapté à la course, l’escalade, l’équitation, la filature, la dissimulation et l’embuscade.

Une Race sans société propre

Ils ne disposent pas de royaume, de langue ancestrale, de religion autonome ou de familles reconnues. Leur existence est organisée par la forteresse, l’armée et le commandant qui les emploient. Ils peuvent néanmoins développer camaraderie d’unité, rivalités entre compagnies, rites militaires et fidélité personnelle à un chef.

Ils ne connaissent pas de mariage traditionnel et ne se reproduisent que lorsqu’une puissance extérieure organise cette reproduction. Les jeunes sont probablement élevés collectivement et séparés selon leurs aptitudes et leur fonction future.

Rapport aux autres Trolls

Ils évitent généralement les Trolls sauvages et entretiennent des rivalités avec les Olog-hai. Ils peuvent les considérer comme des brutes lentes, tandis que les Olog-hai méprisent leur sang humain et leur taille réduite.

Leur corps et leur formation les destinent à protéger un maître, bloquer un passage, poursuivre un assassin, écraser une révolte ou terroriser une population. Les plus expérimentés peuvent commander compagnies orcs, mercenaires variags, garnisons et troupes de siège.

Ils sont brutaux, peu curieux, lourdement conditionnés, économes de leurs efforts hors du combat et cruels envers ceux qu’ils dominent. Ils valorisent force, rang, victoire, équipement, approbation du maître et peur inspirée.

Ils ne possèdent aucune religion autonome mais sont instruits dans les rites de l’Ombre et peuvent servir Sauron, un Nazgûl ou un sorcier. Ils parlent le Parler Noir et le westron, puis peuvent apprendre varadja, haradaïque et orquien.

Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Half-trolls, called Pertorog in the singular and Pirtereg in the plural, are descended from the crossing of Olog-hai and Variag bloodlines. Smaller and faster than Black Trolls, they have a vaguely human silhouette and an intelligence theoretically comparable to that of Men.

They are designed as elite guards, executioners, champions and war leaders in the service of a power of the Shadow. Their appearance is chiefly associated with the final phases of the Third Age.

A creation in the service of the Shadow

They do not seem to have arisen spontaneously as an independent people. Their existence is the result of selection or a breeding programme imposed by Sauron, sorcerers, black priests or Variag lords. This origin explains their physical uniformity, the absence of a truly independent society and the military equipment supplied by their masters.

Difference from the Olog-hai

Olog-hai are larger, heavier and designed to smash battle lines. Half-trolls are faster, more agile, more human in their proportions and better suited to command, guard duty or specialised missions.

Appearance

Men average about 2.16 m in height and women about 2.08 m. They possess extremely broad shoulders, massive torsos, powerful arms, long legs, enormous hands and dense bones.

Their skin is deep black and naturally protective. Their eyes glow an intense red, their tongue is long and pointed, their brow low, their nose broad and their jaw heavily developed.

Longevity and endurance

They generally live between 300 and 500 years, although war and purges often cut their lives short. Their endurance is average relative to their mass but remains impressive by human standards: full armour, heavy loads, long battles and prolonged defence.

Resistance to injury

Their mass, thick bones, skin and musculature reduce the severity of wounds. They are extremely difficult to bring down physically, without possessing exceptional resistance to enchantments, curses, powerful poisons or mental control.

Vision and light

They see remarkably well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. They prefer to avoid brightly lit places but do not automatically fear the Sun and do not turn to stone. A stronger vulnerability to sunlight may be taken as an individual Flaw.

Intelligence and education

The sources describe them both as intelligent and as slow or stupid. This contradiction can be resolved by distinguishing cognitive potential from education: they can learn tactics, languages and command, but they are raised exclusively to serve and discouraged from acting on their own initiative.

Agility

They are relatively fast despite their size. Their bodies are better proportioned than those of Olog-hai and adapted to running, climbing, riding, shadowing, concealment and ambush.

A Race without a society of its own

They possess no kingdom, ancestral language, independent religion or recognised families. Their existence is organised by the fortress, army and commander that employ them. They can nevertheless develop unit camaraderie, rivalries between companies, military rites and personal loyalty to a leader.

Absence of marriage

They know no traditional marriage and reproduce only when an outside power organises that reproduction. The young are probably raised collectively and separated according to their aptitudes and future roles.

Relations with other Trolls

They generally avoid wild Trolls and maintain rivalries with Olog-hai. They may regard them as slow brutes, while Olog-hai despise their human blood and smaller size.

Bodyguards, Executioners and leaders

Their bodies and training suit them to protecting a master, blocking a passage, pursuing an assassin, crushing a revolt or terrorising a population. The most experienced can command Orc companies, Variag mercenaries, garrisons and siege troops.

Temperament

They are brutal, incurious, heavily conditioned, sparing of effort outside combat and cruel toward those they dominate. They value strength, rank, victory, equipment, their master's approval and the fear they inspire.

Possibility of emancipation

A player character requires an exceptional break: military defeat, destruction of the fortress, death of the commander, betrayal, abandonment or the gradual birth of an independent will. Such emancipation does not automatically turn the character into an ally of the Free Peoples.

Religion and languages

They possess no independent religion but are instructed in the rites of the Shadow and may serve Sauron, a Nazgûl or a sorcerer. They speak the Black Speech and Westron, and may later learn Varadja, Haradaic and Orcish.

Relations

They particularly hate Dwarves, who can withstand their charge and pierce their skin. The Variags represent their human heritage without recognising them as kin. Orcs fear them as officers and executioners. Men almost always see them as monsters or living weapons.

Clothing and armour

They wear black tunics, belts, bracers, boots and cloaks. All types of armour are available to them, especially custom-forged harnesses of black metal. Their natural skin further reinforces this protection.

Weapons and fighting style

They can wield axes, swords, composite bows, crossbows, flails, halberds, javelins, maces, hammers, whips and two-handed weapons, often in oversized versions.

They fight as heavy soldiers but are more mobile than Olog-hai: line-breakers, gate guards, champions, commanders, protectors of officers and counter-attack troops.

Riding and craftsmanship

They may use powerful horses, camels of Khand or monstrous mounts able to bear their weight. They learn metalwork, leatherwork, fletching, weapon maintenance and armour repair.

Skills and Talents

Their training covers manoeuvring in armour, weapons, climbing, riding, tracking, ambush, shadowing, concealment, observation, Body Development, wrestling, sprinting, leadership, interrogation and tactics. Their mystical abilities are limited and mainly defensive.

Profession

They normally produce only Fighters. The most natural specialisations correspond to the roles of Mercenary, Heavy Scout or Soldier. This restriction should be preserved unless the GM explicitly decides otherwise.

A Race without a society of its own

Half-trolls possess no kingdom, independent ancestral language, religion of their own or autonomous family traditions. Their existence is organised by the fortress that houses them, the army that employs them and the officer who commands them. Une création au service de l’Ombre

Ils ne semblent pas avoir émergé spontanément comme peuple autonome. Longévité et endurance

Ils vivent généralement entre 300 et 500 ans, bien que leur existence soit souvent écourtée par la guerre et les purges. Leur endurance est moyenne relativement à leur masse, mais reste impressionnante selon les standards humains : armure complète, lourdes charges, longues batailles et défense prolongée.

Résistance aux blessures

Leur masse, leur ossature épaisse, leur peau et leur musculature réduisent la gravité des blessures. Ils sont extrêmement difficiles à abattre physiquement, sans bénéficier pour autant d’une résistance exceptionnelle aux enchantements, malédictions, poisons puissants ou contrôles mentaux.

Vision et lumière

Ils voient remarquablement bien dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée dans les ténèbres absolues. Ils préfèrent éviter les lieux vivement éclairés, mais ne craignent pas automatiquement le Soleil et ne se transforment pas en pierre. Une vulnérabilité solaire plus forte peut être prise comme défaut individuel.

Les sources les décrivent à la fois comme intelligents et comme lents ou stupides. Ils peuvent néanmoins développer camaraderie d’unité, rivalités entre compagnies, rites militaires et fidélité personnelle à un chef.

Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Half-trolls, called Pertorog in the singular and Pirtereg in the plural, are descended from the crossing of Olog-hai and Variag bloodlines. Smaller and faster than Black Trolls, they have a vaguely human silhouette and an intelligence theoretically comparable to that of Men.

They are designed as elite guards, executioners, champions and war leaders in the service of a power of the Shadow. Their appearance is chiefly associated with the final phases of the Third Age.

A creation in the service of the Shadow

They do not seem to have arisen spontaneously as an independent people. Their existence is the result of selection or a breeding programme imposed by Sauron, sorcerers, black priests or Variag lords. This origin explains their physical uniformity, the absence of a truly independent society and the military equipment supplied by their masters.

Difference from the Olog-hai

Olog-hai are larger, heavier and designed to smash battle lines. Half-trolls are faster, more agile, more human in their proportions and better suited to command, guard duty or specialised missions.

Appearance

Men average about 2.16 m in height and women about 2.08 m. They possess extremely broad shoulders, massive torsos, powerful arms, long legs, enormous hands and dense bones.

Their skin is deep black and naturally protective. Their eyes glow an intense red, their tongue is long and pointed, their brow low, their nose broad and their jaw heavily developed.

Longevity and endurance

They generally live between 300 and 500 years, although war and purges often cut their lives short. Their endurance is average relative to their mass but remains impressive by human standards: full armour, heavy loads, long battles and prolonged defence.

Resistance to injury

Their mass, thick bones, skin and musculature reduce the severity of wounds. They are extremely difficult to bring down physically, without possessing exceptional resistance to enchantments, curses, powerful poisons or mental control.

Vision and light

They see remarkably well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. They prefer to avoid brightly lit places but do not automatically fear the Sun and do not turn to stone. A stronger vulnerability to sunlight may be taken as an individual Flaw.

Intelligence and education

The sources describe them both as intelligent and as slow or stupid. This contradiction can be resolved by distinguishing cognitive potential from education: they can learn tactics, languages and command, but they are raised exclusively to serve and discouraged from acting on their own initiative.

Agility

They are relatively fast despite their size. Their bodies are better proportioned than those of Olog-hai and adapted to running, climbing, riding, shadowing, concealment and ambush.

A Race without a society of its own

They possess no kingdom, ancestral language, independent religion or recognised families. Their existence is organised by the fortress, army and commander that employ them. They can nevertheless develop unit camaraderie, rivalries between companies, military rites and personal loyalty to a leader.

Absence of marriage

They know no traditional marriage and reproduce only when an outside power organises that reproduction. The young are probably raised collectively and separated according to their aptitudes and future roles.

Relations with other Trolls

They generally avoid wild Trolls and maintain rivalries with Olog-hai. They may regard them as slow brutes, while Olog-hai despise their human blood and smaller size.

Bodyguards, Executioners and leaders

Their bodies and training suit them to protecting a master, blocking a passage, pursuing an assassin, crushing a revolt or terrorising a population. The most experienced can command Orc companies, Variag mercenaries, garrisons and siege troops.

Temperament

They are brutal, incurious, heavily conditioned, sparing of effort outside combat and cruel toward those they dominate. They value strength, rank, victory, equipment, their master's approval and the fear they inspire.

Possibility of emancipation

A player character requires an exceptional break: military defeat, destruction of the fortress, death of the commander, betrayal, abandonment or the gradual birth of an independent will. Such emancipation does not automatically turn the character into an ally of the Free Peoples.

Religion and languages

They possess no independent religion but are instructed in the rites of the Shadow and may serve Sauron, a Nazgûl or a sorcerer. They speak the Black Speech and Westron, and may later learn Varadja, Haradaic and Orcish.

Relations

They particularly hate Dwarves, who can withstand their charge and pierce their skin. The Variags represent their human heritage without recognising them as kin. Orcs fear them as officers and executioners. Men almost always see them as monsters or living weapons.

Clothing and armour

They wear black tunics, belts, bracers, boots and cloaks. All types of armour are available to them, especially custom-forged harnesses of black metal. Their natural skin further reinforces this protection.

Weapons and fighting style

They can wield axes, swords, composite bows, crossbows, flails, halberds, javelins, maces, hammers, whips and two-handed weapons, often in oversized versions.

Une création au service de l’Ombre

Ils ne semblent pas avoir émergé spontanément comme peuple autonome. Leur existence résulte d’une sélection ou d’un programme de reproduction imposé par Sauron, des sorciers, des prêtres noirs ou des seigneurs variags. Différence avec les Olog-hai

Les Olog-hai sont plus grands, lourds et conçus pour briser les lignes. Les Demi-Trolls sont plus rapides, plus agiles, plus humains dans leurs proportions et mieux adaptés au commandement, à la garde ou aux missions spécialisées.

Apparence

Longévité et endurance

Ils vivent généralement entre 300 et 500 ans, bien que leur existence soit souvent écourtée par la guerre et les purges. Leur endurance est moyenne relativement à leur masse, mais reste impressionnante selon les standards humains : armure complète, lourdes charges, longues batailles et défense prolongée.

Résistance aux blessures

Leur masse, leur ossature épaisse, leur peau et leur musculature réduisent la gravité des blessures. Ils sont extrêmement difficiles à abattre physiquement, sans bénéficier pour autant d’une résistance exceptionnelle aux enchantements, malédictions, poisons puissants ou contrôles mentaux.

Vision et lumière

Intelligence et éducation

Les sources les décrivent à la fois comme intelligents et comme lents ou stupides. They are designed as elite guards, executioners, champions and war leaders in the service of a power of the Shadow. Their appearance is chiefly associated with the final phases of the Third Age.

They do not seem to have arisen spontaneously as an independent people. Their existence is the result of selection or a breeding programme imposed by Sauron, sorcerers, black priests or Variag lords. This origin explains their physical uniformity, the absence of a truly independent society and the military equipment supplied by their masters.

They see remarkably well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. They prefer to avoid brightly lit places but do not automatically fear the Sun and do not turn to stone. A stronger vulnerability to sunlight may be taken as an individual Flaw.

Ils sont conçus comme gardes d’élite, exécuteurs, champions et chefs de guerre au service d’une puissance de l’Ombre. Leur apparition est surtout associée aux dernières phases du Troisième Âge.

Une création au service de l’Ombre

Ils ne semblent pas avoir émergé spontanément comme peuple autonome. Leur existence résulte d’une sélection ou d’un programme de reproduction imposé par Sauron, des sorciers, des prêtres noirs ou des seigneurs variags. Cette origine explique leur homogénéité physique, l’absence de véritable société indépendante et leur équipement militaire fourni par leurs maîtres.

Différence avec les Olog-hai

Les Olog-hai sont plus grands, lourds et conçus pour briser les lignes. Les Demi-Trolls sont plus rapides, plus agiles, plus humains dans leurs proportions et mieux adaptés au commandement, à la garde ou aux missions spécialisées.

Apparence

Leur peau est d’un noir profond et naturellement protectrice. Leurs yeux brillent d’un rouge intense, leur langue est longue et pointue, leur front bas, leur nez large et leur mâchoire très développée.

Longévité et endurance

Ils vivent généralement entre 300 et 500 ans, bien que leur existence soit souvent écourtée par la guerre et les purges. Leur endurance est moyenne relativement à leur masse, mais reste impressionnante selon les standards humains : armure complète, lourdes charges, longues batailles et défense prolongée.

Résistance aux blessures

Leur masse, leur ossature épaisse, leur peau et leur musculature réduisent la gravité des blessures. Ils sont extrêmement difficiles à abattre physiquement, sans bénéficier pour autant d’une résistance exceptionnelle aux enchantements, malédictions, poisons puissants ou contrôles mentaux.

Vision et lumière

Ils préfèrent éviter les lieux vivement éclairés, mais ne craignent pas automatiquement le Soleil et ne se transforment pas en pierre. Ils sont relativement rapides malgré leur taille. Leur corps est mieux proportionné que celui des Olog-hai et adapté à la course, l’escalade, l’équitation, la filature, la dissimulation et l’embuscade.

Ils peuvent néanmoins développer camaraderie d’unité, rivalités entre compagnies, rites militaires et fidélité personnelle à un chef.

Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg

Half-trolls, called Pertorog in the singular and Pirtereg in the plural, are descended from the crossing of Olog-hai and Variag bloodlines. Smaller and faster than Black Trolls, they have a vaguely human silhouette and an intelligence theoretically comparable to that of Men.

Olog-hai are larger, heavier and designed to smash battle lines. Half-trolls are faster, more agile, more human in their proportions and better suited to command, guard duty or specialised missions.

Their skin is deep black and naturally protective. Their eyes glow an intense red, their tongue is long and pointed, their brow low, their nose broad and their jaw heavily developed.

Their mass, thick bones, skin and musculature reduce the severity of wounds. They are extremely difficult to bring down physically, without possessing exceptional resistance to enchantments, curses, powerful poisons or mental control.

They see remarkably well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. They prefer to avoid brightly lit places but do not automatically fear the Sun and do not turn to stone. A stronger vulnerability to sunlight may be taken as an individual Flaw.

Intelligence and education

The sources describe them both as intelligent and as slow or stupid. This contradiction can be resolved by distinguishing cognitive potential from education: they can learn tactics, languages and command, but they are raised exclusively to serve and discouraged from acting on their own initiative.

Agility

They are relatively fast despite their size. Their bodies are better proportioned than those of Olog-hai and adapted to running, climbing, riding, shadowing, concealment and ambush.

A Race without a society of its own

They possess no kingdom, ancestral language, independent religion or recognised families. Their existence is organised by the fortress, army and commander that employ them. They can nevertheless develop unit camaraderie, rivalries between companies, military rites and personal loyalty to a leader.

Absence of marriage

They know no traditional marriage and reproduce only when an outside power organises that reproduction. The young are probably raised collectively and separated according to their aptitudes and future roles.

Relations with other Trolls

They generally avoid wild Trolls and maintain rivalries with Olog-hai. They may regard them as slow brutes, while Olog-hai despise their human blood and smaller size.

Bodyguards, Executioners and leaders

Their bodies and training suit them to protecting a master, blocking a passage, pursuing an assassin, crushing a revolt or terrorising a population. The most experienced can command Orc companies, Variag mercenaries, garrisons and siege troops.

Temperament

They are brutal, incurious, heavily conditioned, sparing of effort outside combat and cruel toward those they dominate. They value strength, rank, victory, equipment, their master's approval and the fear they inspire.

Possibility of emancipation

A player character requires an exceptional break: military defeat, destruction of the fortress, death of the commander, betrayal, abandonment or the gradual birth of an independent will. Such emancipation does not automatically turn the character into an ally of the Free Peoples.

Religion and languages

They possess no independent religion but are instructed in the rites of the Shadow and may serve Sauron, a Nazgûl or a sorcerer. They speak the Black Speech and Westron, and may later learn Varadja, Haradaic and Orcish.

Relations

They particularly hate Dwarves, who can withstand their charge and pierce their skin. The Variags represent their human heritage without recognising them as kin. Orcs fear them as officers and executioners. Men almost always see them as monsters or living weapons.

Clothing and armour

They wear black tunics, belts, bracers, boots and cloaks. All types of armour are available to them, especially custom-forged harnesses of black metal. Their natural skin further reinforces this protection.

Weapons and fighting style

They can wield axes, swords, composite bows, crossbows, flails, halberds, javelins, maces, hammers, whips and two-handed weapons, often in oversized versions.

They fight as heavy soldiers but are more mobile than Olog-hai: line-breakers, gate guards, champions, commanders, protectors of officers and counter-attack troops.

Riding and craftsmanship

They may use powerful horses, camels of Khand or monstrous mounts able to bear their weight. They learn metalwork, leatherwork, fletching, weapon maintenance and armour repair.

Skills and Talents

Their training covers manoeuvring in armour, weapons, climbing, riding, tracking, ambush, shadowing, concealment, observation, Body Development, wrestling, sprinting, leadership, interrogation and tactics. Their mystical abilities are limited and mainly defensive.

Profession

They normally produce only Fighters. The most natural specialisations correspond to the roles of Mercenary, Heavy Scout or Soldier. This restriction should be preserved unless the GM explicitly decides otherwise.

A Race without a society of its own

Half-trolls possess no kingdom, independent ancestral language, religion of their own or autonomous family traditions. Their existence is organised by the fortress that houses them, the army that employs them and the officer who commands them. They can nevertheless develop shared behaviour within a garrison: rivalries between companies, respect for veterans, division of loot, unit markings, military rites and personal loyalty to a leader.

Absence of marriage

They know no traditional marriage and reproduce only when an outside power organises or imposes that reproduction. They therefore normally have no recognised families, family inheritance or permanent households. Children are probably raised collectively and then separated according to size, aptitude and future function. This absence of family structure does not mean that they are incapable of attachment.

Guards, Executioners and war leaders

The role of bodyguard is particularly suited to their nature: taking a blow meant for their master, blocking a passage, wearing extremely heavy armour, intimidating visitors and fighting several opponents. Executioners are trained to track a target, eliminate a champion, crush a revolt or terrorise a population. The most experienced can lead Orc companies, Variag mercenaries, garrisons, siege troops or units of Trolls.

Possibility of emancipation

A player character necessarily implies that an individual can at least partly break free from an imposed function. Military defeat, the destruction of a fortress, the death of a commander, betrayal or abandonment can create such a rupture. This emancipation does not automatically turn the character into an ally of the Free Peoples: the individual may remain cruel, ambitious and deeply marked by upbringing. Their development may consist in discovering the freedom to choose, loyalty that is not imposed, a personal purpose and an identity distinct from that of their creators.

Specialised equipment

Special items are generally supplied by order of a commander: an enchanted weapon, custom-made black armour, a reinforced shield, a protective talisman, a monstrous mount or equipment against light. This dependence on a powerful organisation is an important limitation: after the fall of a master, a Half-troll may retain exceptional equipment without possessing the means to repair or replace it.

Place in character creation

The Half-trolls — Pertorog / Pirtereg Race becomes available from the late Third Age and may survive into the Fourth Age. It should remain Restricted because of its power, size, association with the Shadow and lack of a society of its own.

The player should specify the master or organisation of origin, the garrison, training, reason for separation, relationship with Variags, Olog-hai and Orcs, maintenance of equipment and the exceptional reason why a group accepts the character's presence.
